title: One-Step Bit Query
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean multitape Turing machine, let $x$ and $v$ be finite Boolean words, and let $o$ assign a Boolean answer to each of two query indices and each Boolean word. If $c$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $v$ whose state is $s$, then, for every $i\in\mathbb N$, one step of the compiled program on input $x$, starting from the encoded configuration with phase set to the bit-query phase, yields the encoded configuration with phase set to the work phase, pending bit $o(1,\langle x,\operatorname{bits}(i)\rangle)$, and left-boundary flag false.
hypotheses_covered: $o$ maps each of the two query indices and each Boolean word to a Boolean answer
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $v$
